strategy.summary: Reproduce gh-15650 by building scipy at the buggy commit edff694ae469 with the PR's test added, then running test_gh_15650_mp (and the companion sanity test) in scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py. The buggy build should fail the hardcoded mpmath reference values at rtol=1e-13 for b=1, small |a|, small x; the fixed build should pass. The defect is in the Cython header _hypergeometric.pxd, so a compiled rebuild is required.

system_packages: a C/C++ and Fortran toolchain supported by scipy at that era
BLAS/LAPACK development libraries as required by the scipy build
build_commands: git clone https://github.com/scipy/scipy.git && cd scipy && git checkout edff694ae469 && git submodule update --init
pip install -r requirements/build.txt (or the build requirements listed in pyproject.toml at edff694ae469)
git apply the PR test diff to scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py
spin build (or pip install -e . --no-build-isolation) so that _hypergeometric.pxd changes are compiled into scipy.special
pinned_because: numpy<2.2: era ceiling (newest numpy at PR date 2024-09-03 was 2.1); era-inferred, not a documented constraint, relied on only to match the era
scipy at edff694ae469: the buggy revision is fixed by the commit itself, so the scipy build comes from the checkout rather than a pinned release; version under test is not stated in the evidence
mpmath: unbounded, no documented constraint; chosen as the current release, used only for the optional numerical probe since the test hardcodes reference values

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/special/tests/test_hypergeometric.py::test_gh_15650_mp (parametrized over 24 (a,b=1,x,expected) cases with |a|<0.25, x in 1e-5..0.1) and test_gh_15650_sanity
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision edff694ae469 with the test patch applied, test_gh_15650_mp fails on at least the small-a, small-x parametrizations because assert_allclose(sc.hyperu(a,1.0,x), expected, rtol=1e-13) raises AssertionError; on the fixed revision (DLMF 13.3.7 branch enabled for b==1, x<1, -0.25<a<0.3) all test_gh_15650_mp cases pass and test_gh_15650_sanity passes.
strategy.numerical_probe: python -c "import scipy.special as sc, mpmath as mp; mp.mp.dps=100; a=0.21581740448533887; x=1e-5; print(sc.hyperu(a,1.0,x), float(mp.hyperu(a,1.0,x)))"  (expect the table value 3.6030558839391325 for the test case; compare buggy vs fixed build)

risks: Trigger region is not settled: the pxd diff uses -0.25<a<0.3 while a discussion proposes abs(a)<1 and abs(x)<1; the test's own region is |a|<0.25, 0<x<1, which is the one to reproduce.
The defect is in _hypergeometric.pxd (Cython), so a stale build directory may keep the buggy code; rebuild or clean the build before trusting either transition.
Version under test is not stated; the buggy commit is taken as edff694ae469 per the task, but the scipy version cannot be confirmed from the evidence.
The reference values use mpmath at 100 digits; the expected values in the test are hardcoded, so the test does not depend on the installed mpmath version, but the probe does.
numpy and matplotlib are not numerically relevant to the transition; the numpy ceiling is era-inferred, not documented.

The buggy error is described as several orders of magnitude, so the 1e-13 threshold should be exceeded on any IEEE platform; if a particular platform or compiler happens to stay within 1e-13 on the buggy revision, the test would not fail there and the transition would not show.
The sanity test only bounds results below 1e3 and may pass on the buggy build; the transition rests on test_gh_15650_mp.
Behaviour under sanitizers or non-x86 architectures is not established by the evidence and cannot be assumed.

oracle.reference_source: mpmath hyperu at 100 digits, values hardcoded in test_gh_15650_mp (script in the test comment)
oracle.why: The test compares against hardcoded mpmath reference values, so the oracle is independent of scipy's own output.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision sc.hyperu for b=1, small |a| and small x returns values differing from the mpmath references by several orders of magnitude, so assert_allclose at rtol=1e-13 raises AssertionError for those parametrizations.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the DLMF 13.3.7 branch applied for b==1, x<1, -0.25<a<0.3, values agree with the hardcoded references within rtol=1e-13 and all test_gh_15650_mp cases pass (expected from the PR, not independently verified here).
